answer: Divergent-Context Challenge-Response. Each identity must answer a challenge seeded by its local state, such as a recent tundra sensor reading or a falcon sighting timestamp. Clones share identical state, so they cannot produce divergent answers without splitting into separate contexts. Verification requires a unique path to a public nadir checkpoint, forcing each clone to pay a fresh registration and latency cost per identity. Attackers thus bear linear per-clone overhead, making mass duplication economically unviable.
